source.title: Investigating Label Noise Sensitivity of Convolutional Neural Networks for Fine Grained Audio Signal Labelling

record.tranche_reason: Extends investigation of label-noise effects to fine-grained audio labeling with convolutional networks; its results do not test the listed random-label fitting versions directly.
record.gate_note: The study varies systematic and random annotation misalignment and reports F-measure results. These are audio labeling performance results, not measurements of fitting completely random labels, training error, or test error at chance. The cited image-label-noise findings are prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study cites the original random-label studies but tests sensitivity to small temporal annotation shifts in audio. It reports validation and test F-measure, without measuring random-label memorization, training fit, corruption-fraction trajectories, or learning order. Its results therefore test none of V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: small systematic and random annotation misalignments have non-negligible effects on CNN performance in fine-grained audio labeling, motivating precise annotation timing.
record.recipe_differences: Audio framewise labeling task with small systematic or random temporal misalignments; it does not use the original random-image-label fitting experiment. The study uses mini-batch stochastic gradient descent with Nesterov momentum and a step-wise learning-rate schedule, with batch size 8.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with labeling function, frame rate, and dataset configuration. The higher frame-rate effect is described as much smaller; Configuration II shows an increase for fc against fa, which the authors suggest may reflect ground-truth alignment issues.

fits_no_version.finding: Small systematic and random temporal annotation shifts produce non-negligible differences in audio-labeling F-measure. Effects are smaller at 100 fps; Configuration II includes an fc improvement that the authors attribute to possible ground-truth alignment problems.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CNN performance in fine-grained audio labeling depends on annotation timing, with sensitivity varying across temporal resolution and dataset configuration.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: The study uses only one fold for the 100 [fps] models because of computational cost. Results for the figures are mostly presented graphically, without uncertainty estimates. The tested misalignments are small temporal annotation shifts in audio, not completely random labels.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and fitting with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction grows.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A corruption-fraction sweep from none to fully random labels, perfect training fit, and test error rising steadily toward chance.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels and how real versus random labels are learned over training.

record.verdict_notes: The study does not vary the fraction of randomly replaced labels or report training-set memorization. Fixed non-architectural hyperparameters alone do not make it a test of V1. Figure 5's extracted number ordering conflicts with the prose; corrected assignments cannot be established confidently from the supplied flattened text.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random training labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence as the fraction of corrupted labels changes.
Fitting shuffled, permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A sweep from no corruption to fully random labels; training-set fit, test error, and whether test error rises toward chance.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on fitting random labels and generalization.
Whether true-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.
